AGAINST FEVER

Take carp and parsley with rue (?), boil them well together, then pound them well and apply as a poultice overnight. In the morning, prepare the pounded mixture and give it warm to the sick person to drink at daybreak, on the day when the fever (attack) would come upon him. Then wash the pounded mixture in water and moisten the sick person's head with it.

Then take red willow leaves, boiled together with young [shoots], boil them well together, then in that water soak and bind the sick person's feet, and then with that same warm leaf-poultice on the feet, so that it draws out (the illness); afterward he should walk about and wander around the house for some time, staying [there] a while, and then lie down and sleep, and he will be healed. Try this remedy. [signed] Master/Priest Bretislav (?)

Item: Another remedy trusted against fever: take rye (?) and mix it well, and give it, ground into powder, warm to the sick person to drink on the day the attack would come upon him. [Attributed to] Jetřich Vsilova (?)
